Prodi Ilmu Komunikasi FISIP UNAS Perluas Kerja Sama Internasional Melalui Program Global Mobility di Malaysia

Rangkaian kegiatan dilaksanakan melalui kunjungan ke Kedutaan Besar Republik Indonesia (KBRI) Malaysia, Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM), UCSI University, serta Sekolah Indonesia Kuala Lumpur (SIKL). Selama kegiatan berlangsung, delegasi UNAS menjajaki peluang kerja sama akademik dan industri yang mendukung peningkatan kualitas pendidikan serta kompetensi mahasiswa di tingkat global.

Dalam setiap pertemuan, delegasi memperkenalkan berbagai pengembangan Program Studi Ilmu Komunikasi FISIP UNAS, mulai dari implementasi kurikulum yang selaras dengan kebutuhan industri, pengembangan Kelas Internasional, hingga program peningkatan kompetensi mahasiswa. Selain itu, pembahasan difokuskan pada peluang kolaborasi dalam bidang pendidikan, pertukaran mahasiswa dan dosen, transfer kredit, penelitian bersama, serta pengabdian kepada masyarakat.

Kunjungan diawali dengan pertemuan bersama Ir. R. Ahmad Romadhoni Surya Putra, S.Pt., M.Sc., Ph.D., IPU., ASEAN Eng., selaku Atase Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan KBRI Malaysia. Dalam pertemuan tersebut, kedua belah pihak membahas peluang kolaborasi yang dapat memperkuat jejaring akademik antara Indonesia dan Malaysia sekaligus membuka kesempatan kerja sama bagi sivitas akademika Universitas Nasional.

Agenda berikutnya adalah kunjungan industri ke Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) yang diterima langsung oleh pimpinan RTM. Dalam pertemuan tersebut, delegasi memperoleh wawasan mengenai perkembangan industri penyiaran di Malaysia, transformasi media digital, strategi komunikasi publik, serta inovasi yang dilakukan RTM dalam menghadapi perubahan perilaku audiens. Kedua institusi juga mendiskusikan peluang kerja sama dalam bentuk kuliah praktisi, program magang, penelitian bersama, dan pengembangan laboratorium penyiaran.

Delegasi kemudian melanjutkan kunjungan ke UCSI University dan diterima oleh pihak pengelola program studi media. Pembahasan difokuskan pada pengembangan kurikulum, pertukaran mahasiswa dan dosen, transfer kredit, penelitian bersama, publikasi ilmiah, serta kolaborasi dalam mendukung pengembangan Kelas Internasional Program Studi Ilmu Komunikasi FISIP UNAS.

Selain memperkuat kemitraan dengan perguruan tinggi dan industri, Prodi Ilmu Komunikasi FISIP UNAS juga melaksanakan kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat di Sekolah Indonesia Kuala Lumpur (SIKL). Kegiatan tersebut diwujudkan melalui workshop bertema Public Speaking yang membekali siswa dengan keterampilan berbicara di depan umum, menyampaikan gagasan secara efektif, membangun rasa percaya diri, serta meningkatkan kemampuan komunikasi dalam kehidupan sehari-hari. Workshop berlangsung secara interaktif melalui praktik, simulasi, dan diskusi bersama peserta.

Dekan FISIP Universitas Nasional menegaskan bahwa kegiatan Global Mobility merupakan bagian dari komitmen fakultas untuk memperluas jejaring internasional dan menghadirkan pengalaman belajar yang lebih luas bagi mahasiswa. Ia berharap kerja sama yang dibangun bersama KBRI Malaysia, RTM, UCSI University, dan SIKL dapat berkembang menjadi program berkelanjutan di bidang pendidikan, penelitian, dan pengabdian kepada masyarakat.

Ketua Program Studi Ilmu Komunikasi FISIP UNAS, Swastiningsih, S.E., M.Si., menambahkan bahwa kerja sama internasional merupakan langkah strategis dalam meningkatkan kualitas pendidikan sekaligus mempersiapkan lulusan yang mampu bersaing di tingkat global.

Sementara itu, Sekretaris Program Studi Ilmu Komunikasi FISIP Universitas Nasional, Cyntia Dewi Anggraini, S.I.Kom., M.I.Kom., menyampaikan bahwa kunjungan ke RTM memberikan perspektif baru mengenai perkembangan industri media. Menurutnya, pengalaman tersebut menjadi masukan berharga dalam pengembangan kurikulum yang relevan dengan kebutuhan industri komunikasi masa kini.

Melalui rangkaian kegiatan tersebut, Program Studi Ilmu Komunikasi FISIP Universitas Nasional kembali menunjukkan komitmennya dalam membangun kolaborasi internasional guna meningkatkan mutu pendidikan, memperluas jejaring akademik dan industri, serta memberikan pengalaman pembelajaran yang lebih luas bagi mahasiswa.(***)

UNDIP, Semarang (23/11) – Inovasi teknologi karya dosen Universitas Diponegoro ( UNDIP ) kembali mendapatkan pengakuan di tingkat internasional. Penelitian kolaboratif yang dikembangkan Mochammad Ariyanto, S.T., M.T., Ph.D. , dosen Departemen Teknik Mesin Fakultas Teknik UNDIP, bersama tim peneliti The University of Osaka, Jepang, terpilih menjadi sampul (cover) jurnal ilmiah internasional bergengsi Device yang diterbitkan Cell Press, Elsevier, Volume 4, Issue 11, edisi 20 November 2026.

Penelitian berjudul “ Biohybrid Navigation through Real-Time Terrain Recognition and Natural Climbing in Cyborg Insects ” ini menghadirkan inovasi sistem navigasi serangga cyborg berbasis kecerdasan buatan ( artificial intelligence/AI ) yang mampu mengenali karakteristik medan secara real-time serta memanfaatkan kemampuan alami serangga untuk melintasi berbagai rintangan.

Capaian tersebut menjadi bukti kontribusi ilmuwan UNDIP dalam pengembangan teknologi robotika mutakhir melalui jejaring riset internasional. Lebih dari sekadar pencapaian akademik, inovasi ini membuka peluang pengembangan teknologi untuk misi pencarian dan penyelamatan korban bencana di wilayah yang sulit dijangkau manusia maupun robot konvensional.

Mochammad Ariyanto merupakan peneliti utama dari UNDIP yang mengembangkan teknologi tersebut melalui kolaborasi bersama tim The University of Osaka di bawah kepemimpinan Prof. Keisuke Morishima. Penelitian ini merupakan bagian dari aktivitas akademiknya sebagai Visiting Academic Staff di Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Osaka, Jepang .

Menggabungkan Kecerdasan Buatan dengan Kemampuan Alami Serangga

Keunggulan penelitian ini terletak pada penggabungan kemampuan biologis serangga dengan teknologi robotika dan kecerdasan buatan.

Dalam sistem konvensional, navigasi serangga cyborg umumnya dirancang untuk menghindari rintangan. Padahal, serangga memiliki kemampuan alami untuk memanjat dan melintasi permukaan yang tidak rata. Pendekatan tersebut kemudian dikembangkan melalui sistem pengenalan medan berbasis AI sehingga gerakan serangga dapat disesuaikan dengan karakteristik lingkungan yang dihadapinya.

Melalui perangkat elektronik miniatur yang dipasang pada tubuh serangga, sistem dapat mengidentifikasi permukaan datar, tanjakan, turunan, hingga lubang secara real-time . Hasil pengujian menunjukkan sistem klasifikasi medan berbasis AI mencapai akurasi 92 persen dalam evaluasi offline .

Kemampuan tersebut memungkinkan sistem mengurangi perintah kendali yang tidak diperlukan ketika serangga sedang memanjat, sehingga pergerakan menjadi lebih efisien dalam menghadapi medan kompleks.

Dalam wawancara yang sebelumnya dipublikasikan melalui kanal resmi UNDIP, Ariyanto menjelaskan bahwa pendekatan biohybrid dipilih karena memungkinkan peneliti memanfaatkan keunggulan biologis serangga tanpa harus menciptakan seluruh sistem pergerakan secara mekanis.

“Kalau kita memaksa membuat robot sepenuhnya mekatronik dengan ukuran sangat kecil, tantangannya jauh lebih kompleks. Maka pendekatan ini justru memanfaatkan keunggulan alami serangga sambil tetap memastikan kelangsungan hidupnya terjaga,” jelas Ariyanto dalam wawancara UNDIP yang dipublikasikan pada September 2025.

Sementara itu, Prof. Keisuke Morishima dari The University of Osaka, dalam publikasi resmi universitasnya pada Agustus 2026, menjelaskan bahwa tantangan utama penelitian adalah mengembangkan sistem yang mampu mengenali kondisi medan secara langsung tanpa mengganggu kemampuan gerak alami serangga.

Morishima menyebut pendekatan yang dikembangkan tim sebagai biohybrid physical AI , yakni integrasi kecerdasan buatan dengan kemampuan fisik organisme hidup untuk menghasilkan sistem navigasi otonom yang lebih efisien.

Berpotensi Mendukung Teknologi Penyelamatan Korban Bencana

Inovasi serangga cyborg memiliki prospek pengembangan untuk operasi pencarian dan penyelamatan ( search and rescue ), khususnya di lokasi bencana dengan akses terbatas, seperti celah reruntuhan bangunan dan area yang terlalu sempit bagi robot konvensional.

Bagi Indonesia yang memiliki tingkat kerawanan bencana tinggi, pengembangan teknologi ini menjadi relevan untuk mendukung sistem penanggulangan bencana berbasis inovasi.

Dalam wawancara UNDIP sebelumnya, Ariyanto juga menyampaikan optimismenya terhadap potensi pemanfaatan teknologi tersebut di Indonesia.

“Saya yakin teknologi ini dapat membantu misi penyelamatan di Indonesia, terutama di wilayah perkotaan padat penduduk,” ungkapnya.

Potensi penerapan teknologi ini juga telah mendapatkan perhatian Badan Nasional Penanggulangan Bencana (BNPB). Pada Mei 2026, tim Cyborg Insect UNDIP diundang untuk mendemonstrasikan teknologi kecoa robot dalam simulasi pencarian korban bencana. Kegiatan tersebut sekaligus membuka peluang kolaborasi pengembangan inovasi teknologi kebencanaan.

Meski demikian, teknologi navigasi yang dipublikasikan dalam jurnal Device masih merupakan hasil pengembangan dan pengujian riset. Pemanfaatannya secara operasional dalam misi penyelamatan nyata memerlukan pengembangan serta validasi lebih lanjut.

Memperkuat Reputasi dan Kolaborasi Riset Internasional UNDIP

Keberhasilan penelitian UNDIP bersama The University of Osaka menjadi sampul jurnal Device memperlihatkan kapasitas peneliti Indonesia untuk berkontribusi dalam pengembangan ilmu pengetahuan dan teknologi pada tingkat global.

Device merupakan jurnal ilmiah internasional terbitan Cell Press yang berfokus pada pengembangan perangkat, rekayasa, dan inovasi teknologi lintas disiplin. Terpilihnya penelitian tersebut sebagai sampul edisi November 2026 memberikan visibilitas internasional yang semakin luas bagi karya ilmiah yang melibatkan UNDIP.

Penelitian ini juga telah menarik perhatian sejumlah media dan portal sains internasional, termasuk Science Magazine, EurekAlert!, TechXplore, dan Asia Research News.

Bagi UNDIP, pencapaian tersebut sekaligus memperkuat kerja sama strategis dengan perguruan tinggi internasional dalam pengembangan penelitian unggulan, khususnya bidang robotika, kecerdasan buatan, dan teknologi biohybrid.

Kolaborasi ini menunjukkan bahwa internasionalisasi perguruan tinggi tidak hanya diwujudkan melalui mobilitas akademik, tetapi juga melalui produksi pengetahuan bersama, publikasi ilmiah bereputasi, serta pengembangan inovasi yang berpotensi memberikan manfaat bagi masyarakat.

Sejalan dengan semangat UNDIP Bermartabat, UNDIP Bermanfaat, keberhasilan ini mempertegas komitmen Universitas Diponegoro untuk terus mendorong penelitian berdaya saing global yang tidak hanya menghasilkan pengakuan akademik, tetapi juga menawarkan solusi terhadap tantangan nyata yang dihadapi masyarakat. (Komunikasi Publik/UNDIP)

Menteri Agama Nasaruddin Umar menutup Olimpiade Madrasah Indonesia (OMI) 2026 di Asrama Haji Pondok Gede, Jakarta Timur. Di hadapan ratusan finalis dari 34 provinsi, Menag mengajak pelajar madrasah menghidupkan kembali tradisi kejayaan sains dan teknologi peradaban Islam seperti era Madrasah Baitul Hikmah.

Menteri Agama Nasaruddin Umar mengenang sosok almarhum Prof. KH. Syukron Ma’mun sebagai ulama yang tidak hanya memiliki keluasan ilmu, tetapi juga mengamalkan ilmu yang dimilikinya dalam kehidupan sehari-hari.

Kepala Madrasah Aliyah Negeri (MAN) 2 Kota Makassar, Darmawati, meraih Juara I kategori Guru dan Tenaga Kependidikan (GTK) Dedikatif tingkat nasional pada ajang Anugerah GTK Kemenag Tahun 2026. Penghargaan tersebut diberikan bertepatan dengan puncak rangkaian Hari Guru Nasional (HGN) Kementerian Agama yang digelar di Pelataran Masjid Istiqlal, Jakarta.

Direktorat Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) Kementerian Agama menggelar Lomba Apresiasi Guru dan Pengawas PAI sebagai rangkaian peringatan Hari Guru Nasional (HGN) 2026. Pendaftaran yang dibuka dari 16 – 22 November 2026 banjir peminat hingga mencapai 851 pendaftar.

Kementerian Agama menyiapkan langkah tindak lanjut atas Peraturan Presiden (Perpres) Nomor 111 Tahun 2025 melalui penguatan materi pendidikan dan penyusunan naskah akademik serta rancangan undang-undang (RUU). Upaya tersebut diarahkan untuk membangun pemahaman dan kesadaran peserta didik di lingkungan pendidikan Kemenag mengenai isu LGBTQ.

Inspektorat Jenderal Kementerian Agama memperkuat pengawasan tata kelola Program Makan Bergizi Gratis (MBG) di madrasah. Pengawasan difokuskan pada lima area strategis, yakni akurasi data penerima manfaat, keamanan pangan dan kecukupan gizi, distribusi makanan, akuntabilitas, serta kesiapsiagaan menghadapi keadaan darurat.

Ferrari has unveiled the new 296 Challenge Stradale and 296 Challenge Evo, two V6 performance cars that go without hybrid assistance. The Evo delivers 700 hp from its engine alone, while the Stradale gives you race-derived gearshift control alongside equipment such as adaptive cruise control. Their differences go beyond engine output, with distinct gearbox calibrations, aerodynamic setups and braking controls shaping how each responds to its driver. You’ll discover how those choices bring racing character to the Stradale and give Evo drivers more ways to adapt to different circuits.

Road and race: Ferrari developed the road-legal 296 Challenge Stradale alongside the 296 Challenge Evo race car. Engine output: Both use a non-hybrid 2,992 cc twin-turbo V6, producing 670 hp in the Stradale and 700 hp in the Evo. Stradale performance: Ferrari rates the Stradale for 0-100 km/h in 2.8 seconds. Stradale downforce: The Stradale produces 617 kg of downforce at 250 km/h, 72% more than the 296 GTB. Evo debut: The Evo is expected to debut in Europe and North America in 2027, with regional series following in 2028.

Ferrari developed the road-legal 296 Challenge Stradale alongside the 296 Challenge Evo, a race car for the Ferrari Challenge Trofeo Pirelli. The Evo builds on the 296 Challenge, which has competed since 2024, while the Stradale adapts its racing relative’s design for road-car safety and practical requirements.

Both cars were unveiled on November 21, 2026 at the Ferrari Finali Mondiali in Montmeló, Spain.

Both cars use a 2,992 cc twin-turbo V6 with a 120-degree layout and no hybrid assistance. The Stradale drives its rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox, while the Evo uses a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission.

At 140 kg less than the 296 GTB’s stated dry weight, the Stradale has a weight-to-power ratio of 1.98 kg/hp. Ferrari rates it for 0-100 km/h in 2.8 seconds, 0-200 km/h in 7.9 seconds and a top speed above 300 km/h.

The Stradale’s engine and turbochargers draw on the 296 Challenge. Ferrari says revised boost and valve-timing management increases dynamic torque by more than 32% over the 296 GTB for the same maneuver, while enlarged exhaust outlets reduce back pressure.

At high loads and revs, race-derived gearbox logic delivers upshifts in around 170 milliseconds; at low and medium revs, a different calibration shifts in around 250 milliseconds. A system carries engine pressure waves into the cabin, and Ferrari offers a separate exhaust for track use that dealerships can fit and remove.

The Stradale produces 617 kg of downforce at 250 km/h, 72% more than the 296 GTB. Its fixed rear wing contributes 270 kg at that speed, working with a splitter, enclosed underbody, diffusers, and vortex generators.

Road use, including speed bumps, shaped the front underbody, while ducts called aerodampers reduce changes in downforce as the car pitches. Radiators ahead of the front wheels send hot air out through the bonnet and toward the windscreen and roof.

Ferrari says the Stradale’s suspension setup increases maximum lateral performance by 7%, improves stability by 34% and reduces roll gradient by 68% compared with the 296 GTB. Semi-active dampers control changes in ride height and balance, and Pirelli developed P Zero R and P Zero Trofeo RS tires specifically for the car.

ABS Evo uses sensor data to guide braking across all grip conditions and Manettino settings, which range from Wet to ESC Off. Braking calibration changes from Race mode onwards, while suspension calibration becomes more performance-focused from Sport.

Carbon-ceramic discs measure 398 × 38 mm at the front and 380 × 34 mm at the rear. Ferrari designed the brake pedal to evoke the Evo’s feel, with reduced travel under heavy deceleration.

You can specify the cabin with trim removed beneath the seats and center console, exposing part of the chassis. Optional carbon-fiber tubular seats weigh 25% less than standard racing seats, while optional forged wheels reduce unsprung mass by approximately 11.9 kg.

Road equipment includes adaptive cruise control, lane assistance, blind-spot detection and automatic emergency braking for vehicles, pedestrians and cyclists. Front and rear cameras assist maneuvering, and assistance functions can be configured through the instrument cluster.

Ferrari says the Evo produces 12% more maximum downforce than the 296 Challenge, equivalent to an extra 100 kg at 250 km/h. Its Low Drag configuration reduces drag by 4%, using a lower rear-wing angle and removing front aerodynamic elements.

A wider wing adjustment range, revised diffuser, new mirrors and carbon-fiber components expand the setup options for different circuits. A cooled high-performance driveshaft also supports more extreme setups, while raising the rear ride height by up to 10 mm adds approximately 30 kg of downforce at 250 km/h.

In Ferrari’s comparison, the Evo in High Downforce configuration lapped Mugello 0.8 seconds faster than the 296 Challenge. Ferrari attributes the improvement to aerodynamic and vehicle-dynamics changes informed by driver and team feedback.

Revised traction control and electronic differential settings are intended to improve braking stability and agility through fast corners. The brake pedal has more travel and requires more force for the same deceleration, while the redesigned display shows control intervention, tire-pressure data and lap times.

Two switches, TC1 and TC2, each offer five traction-control settings, and four ABS settings cover performance and stability in dry and wet conditions. Optional equipment includes a removable passenger seat, a silencer for noise-restricted circuits and an LTE antenna for Race Control messages.

We think leaving out the hybrid system is the most telling choice. It keeps weight and complexity down, and the Stradale’s 1,330 kg dry weight, 140 kg below the 296 GTB, gives that decision substance. Its racing engine roots, fixed rear wing and brake pedal designed to evoke the Evo’s feel reinforce what we see as Ferrari’s aim: a road car that feels like a race car, not just a faster version of the usual one.

The Evo is expected to make its racing debut in 2027 in the Europe and North America series, with regional series following from 2028. The LTE antenna is expected to be mandatory for Ferrari Challenge entries. For the Stradale, Ferrari’s seven-year maintenance program covers scheduled servicing every 20,000 km or annually, while fuel-consumption and emissions figures are pending homologation.

Paying flagship prices without getting flagship memory is the central concern surrounding the rumoured Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra, a device Samsung has not yet announced or confirmed. According to a video breakdown from Techtics and related hardware leaks, Samsung may reserve next-generation memory standards for higher-storage tiers while charging more for larger capacities. As with any unannounced smartphone and pre-release software, hardware configurations, pricing, and launch timelines remain subject to change.

Selective rollout: A leak indicates only three of ten Galaxy S27 lineup configurations get next-generation RAM and storage, all starting at 512GB. Ultra storage tiers: The rumoured 256GB Galaxy S27 Ultra uses LPDDR5X and UFS 4.1, while 512GB and 1TB models move to LPDDR6 and UFS 5.0. Theoretical vs. daily speed: Newer storage reportedly delivers more than double the sequential read speed on paper, though real-world gains may feel more modest. Pricing pressure: Rising memory costs could push Galaxy S27 pricing higher, especially on 512GB and 1TB variants. One UI 9.5 shifts: Early S27 builds reportedly reposition the Now Bar around the front camera, while One UI 9.5 beta code for the Galaxy S26 hints at selfie leveling.

Samsung has not officially unveiled the Galaxy S27 Ultra as the successor to the Galaxy S26 Ultra. However, recent supply-chain reports suggest that picking a capacity tier on the Galaxy S27 series could determine which memory generation your phone actually runs.

Tiered storage hardware is not new for Samsung. Entry-level 128GB variants of past Galaxy S models—such as select Galaxy S23 and Galaxy S24 configurations—used slower flash storage than higher-capacity siblings. If the latest rumours hold up, that same capacity-based split could return at a higher tier on the Galaxy S27 lineup.

A report originating from Korean tipster leaks indicates that only three of ten total configurations across the Galaxy S27 family will pair LPDDR6 RAM with UFS 5.0 storage, with all three starting at 512GB or higher. Under this reported split, buyers who pick the base storage tier on the Ultra would get last-generation memory standards instead:

Techtics notes that giving the entry 256GB Galaxy S27 Ultra the same generation of RAM and storage found on the standard Galaxy S27 is tough to justify at Ultra pricing. Even though UFS 5.0 is rated for sequential read speeds well over double those of earlier standards on paper, everyday tasks like opening apps or scrolling social feeds often show smaller day-to-day differences than synthetic benchmarks suggest.

Chipset differences across the lineup could add another layer of complexity for prospective buyers. While the Galaxy S27 Ultra is rumoured to rely on a Snapdragon processor across regions, the Galaxy S27 Pro has surfaced in benchmarks and leaks with Samsung’s unannounced Exynos 2700 chip in select markets.

Reports indicate that the Exynos 2700 supports LPDDR6 memory, whereas the Snapdragon option paired with certain S27 Pro variants may not run the newer RAM at full speed. The same leak highlights a 1TB Exynos Galaxy S27 Pro with 16GB of RAM receiving the faster memory standard, meaning regional silicon choices could create noticeable spec gaps even within the same model name.

Rising component costs—driven heavily by broader memory demand across the tech industry—are widely cited as the reason Samsung could restrict LPDDR6 and UFS 5.0 to select configurations. Rather than absorbing higher bill-of-materials costs across every unit, limiting the newest memory to 512GB and 1TB tiers could help keep entry prices from climbing even higher.

Pricing context from the current generation makes that trade-off harder to ignore. After Samsung raised the US starting price of the Galaxy S26 Ultra to $1,399.99 in October 2026—with holiday discounts bringing it down to around $1,049—any further increase on 512GB and 1TB S27 Ultra models would add meaningful upfront cost. In the past, Samsung frequently offered free storage upgrades during pre-orders (such as 512GB for the price of 256GB), though that promotion was dropped for the Galaxy S26 in the US. If a free-storage pre-order perk does not return for the Galaxy S27 Ultra, jumping to 512GB will require paying full price for the extra capacity.

Beyond silicon and storage, early software reports point to visual changes in Samsung’s One UI 9.5 interface. Internal builds associated with the Galaxy S27 reportedly shift the Now Bar toward the center of the display around the front camera cutout, creating a pill-style presentation reminiscent of Apple’s Dynamic Island.

That camera-centered Now Bar layout has not appeared in initial One UI 9.5 beta builds rolling out for the Galaxy S26 series, and Android rivals such as Realme, OPPO, and Xiaomi have already experimented with similar live-activity cutouts. Because One UI 9.5 is currently in beta testing on existing devices, final interface behaviour on the Galaxy S27 lineup could still evolve before release.

Software sleuths digging into One UI 9.5 beta code for the Galaxy S26 have also spotted clues about a Horizontal Lock feature aimed at keeping selfie videos level while you walk or move. Much of the broader One UI 9.5 feature set—which already includes tools like native app locking, updated camera controls, and health additions in beta builds—is expected to reach eligible older Galaxy models alongside or after the next flagship launch.

Camera enthusiasts are also watching Expert RAW, which is rumoured to be getting a refresh featuring a 30-shot RAW burst mode and a wider simulated aperture effect. Whether those camera tools arrive on time for launch or roll out later remains unconfirmed.

If the reported memory split is accurate, getting the newest RAM and storage on a Galaxy S27 Ultra will depend on choosing a 512GB or 1TB model rather than relying on the Ultra badge alone. Watch the exact pricing tiers and whether Samsung brings back pre-order storage upgrades before setting a budget, as waiting for a higher-capacity S27 Ultra—or shopping discounted Galaxy S26 Ultra deals—could be the deciding factor. Remember that the Galaxy S27 Ultra and One UI 9.5 remain unannounced or in pre-release testing, so specifications, pricing, and availability remain subject to change.

Video tests put the vivo X500 Pro Max smartphone and Insta360 Luna Ultra gimbal camera through walking shots, low-light scenes and slow motion. As The Film Alliance explains, the Luna Ultra’s detachable touchscreen lets you monitor footage with the camera facing away, while the phone’s larger screen is harder to see in that position. Take a closer look at how they render skin and outdoor colors, and see what happens when indoor lighting causes background flicker.

Both cameras record 8K video, with the vivo costing around $1,500 on eBay and the Luna Ultra starting at $769. The vivo records slow motion at 4K 240fps, while the Luna Ultra reaches 240fps at 1080p. In low-light walking footage, the Luna Ultra’s three-axis gimbal produced steadier video than the vivo. The Luna Ultra produced a cleaner moon shot at ISO 6400, with less noise and no jumping ghost flare. In a sunrise time-lapse, the vivo adjusted exposure faster than the Luna Ultra with both cameras set to auto exposure.

The vivo X500 Pro Max and Insta360 Luna Ultra both record 8K video, but their stabilization approaches differ. In a low-light walking comparison, the Luna Ultra produced steadier footage. The vivo offered higher-resolution slow motion and adjusted exposure faster in a sunrise time-lapse.

The vivo is a smartphone with three rear cameras co-engineered with ZEISS. It cost around $1,500 on eBay and had not been released in the US at the time of the comparison. The Luna Ultra is a compact, dual-lens gimbal camera co-engineered by Insta360 and Leica, and it starts at $769. The Film Alliance bought both for the comparison rather than receiving them from the makers.

On the vivo, the cameras comprise a 24mm-equivalent main camera, an 85mm telephoto with 3.5× optical zoom and a 15mm ultrawide. The main camera has the largest sensor of the three. The Luna Ultra pairs a 1-inch main sensor and 20mm-equivalent lens with a 60mm telephoto.

Both cameras have fixed apertures and let you adjust resolution, frame rate, shutter speed and ISO. The Luna Ultra offers an ISO range of 100 to 6400 and white balance from 2000K to 10000K.

The vivo X500 Pro Max can record slow motion at 4K 240fps, while the Luna Ultra reaches 240fps at 1080p. Despite the phone’s resolution advantage, The Film Alliance preferred the Luna Ultra’s slow-motion footage: its 1080p footage had more natural-looking color, while the vivo’s white balance looked off across the shots.

In another shot, the vivo showed a stronger yellow tint, although its footage had better resolution. The Film Alliance suggests the Luna Ultra’s larger sensor might account for its appearance in slow motion.

At its other settings, the Luna Ultra records 8K at up to 30fps in 16:9 or 2.35:1, and 4K at up to 120fps. In 8K landscape recording it supports 1× to 6× zoom.

The Luna Ultra produced noticeably steadier footage in the low-light walking comparison. The vivo X500 Pro Max showed more shake and bounce, even though both cameras used the same steady walking motion.

For stabilization, the Luna Ultra combines a three-axis mechanical gimbal with electronic stabilization, though the gimbal does not counter up-and-down movement. The vivo uses optical stabilization on its main and telephoto cameras. Vivo claims CIPA 7.0 stabilization for both in laboratory conditions and lists three degrees of optical stabilization for the main camera, which it describes as having gimbal-style stabilization.

In low light, the vivo also showed a moving ghost flare that the Luna Ultra did not. The Film Alliance rated the phone’s stabilization above an iPhone’s, but found the flare potentially distracting.

The Luna Ultra produced a cleaner moon shot at ISO 6400, with less noise and no jumping ghost flare around the moon. The vivo also showed a smearing effect around lights after a check found its lens clean. The Luna Ultra gave a more gradual transition between bright and dark areas.

In another low-light scene, with both cameras on auto white balance, the difference was much smaller: the vivo’s image was a little brighter. A further comparison, with the cameras exposed as closely as possible, also showed little difference.

For low light, the Luna Ultra has a dedicated PureVideo mode at up to 4K 60fps. Insta360 and Leica claim up to 14 stops of dynamic range for the camera, and Vivo claims 17 EV for the X500 Pro Max’s main camera in Log mode. In real shooting, The Film Alliance could not tell the two apart on dynamic range.

The vivo X500 Pro Max produced more realistic-looking skin in one lighting environment. With both cameras on their standard color profiles, the phone rendered skin slightly more saturated, while the Luna Ultra made it look drained. In a different indoor talking-head shot, both handled the skin tone well.

That indoor shot revealed background flicker on the vivo, which you could correct with shutter speed, while the Luna Ultra compensated automatically in the same scene.

Outside in good light, the Luna Ultra produced richer colors, particularly in a flag, while the vivo appeared slightly less saturated. The phone’s sky was greenish blue and looked more realistic; the Luna Ultra’s shifted toward purple. Foliage also differed, with lighter, yellower greens on the vivo and more lime green on the Luna Ultra. The difference was visible with both cameras fully zoomed in.

With both cameras on auto white balance, the vivo shifted warmer and more orange, while the Luna Ultra looked closer to the scene as seen by eye. In a sunlit shot, the vivo’s lens reflection resembled a starburst, whereas the Luna Ultra rendered a softer sun with a green flare moving through the frame.

For footage that needs color work after recording, the vivo supports Cinematic Pro Log Video. The Luna Ultra records 10-bit video with Standard, Dolby Vision and I-Log profiles, plus Leica Natural, Leica Vivid and Leica Chrome image profiles.

The vivo X500 Pro Max handled the sunrise time-lapse more smoothly, changing exposure quickly as the light increased. With both cameras set to auto exposure, the Luna Ultra took much longer to adjust.

The Luna Ultra’s detachable 2-inch OLED touchscreen works as a remote and includes a microphone, so you can monitor a shot with the camera facing away. The vivo has a larger screen that you cannot readily view when the phone faces away.

We think stabilization is the difference worth watching for. Both cameras shoot 8K, but sharp footage is wasted if it shakes. A mechanical gimbal and a phone’s gimbal-style optical stabilization solve the same problem in different ways. We think the Luna Ultra suits people who film on the move and want fewer fixes later. It also automatically compensated for indoor background flicker that needed a shutter-speed correction on the vivo. Anyone unwilling to carry a second device, or who wants one pocket tool for everything, will be happier with the phone.

The Film Alliance would choose the Luna Ultra for a dedicated video camera, favoring its color rendering and detachable screen rather than the convenience of shooting on a phone. Its advantage was clearer while walking than in the closely matched static low-light scenes. The vivo is not outclassed for every use: its higher-resolution slow motion and quicker sunrise exposure changes favor it when those matter more than steady footage on the move.

Large 4K HDR movies played without buffering on the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, which officially launched on November 13, 2026. For anyone still running the original 2017 Apple TV 4K, faster app launches, snappier playback, and modern wireless hardware carry more weight than headline features that can also run on older Apple TV hardware. As covered in a hands-on video breakdown from AppleInsider featured below, upgrading makes the most sense for heavy streamers—though waiting for a discount is worth considering if the $299 retail price feels steep.

Price and storage: The 2026 model starts at $299 with 128GB of storage and Gigabit Ethernet, compared with $179 for 32GB or $199 for 64GB in 2017. Processor and memory: The A19 chip and 8GB of RAM replace the 2017 model’s A10X Fusion processor and 3GB of RAM. Wi-Fi 7 playback: Plex streamed large 4K HDR files without buffering over Wi-Fi 7, though earlier stuttering may also have involved video codec support. Built-in microphones: Three far-field mics enable hands-free Siri requests and help tune HomePod spatial audio. Four-HomePod surround: The 2026 box supports up to four compatible HomePods for surround and whole-room audio.

Apple’s fourth-generation Apple TV 4K arrived on November 13, 2026, pairing a major silicon jump, built-in microphones, and 128GB of storage against a box that originally debuted in September 2017.

At $299, the 2026 model ships in a single 128GB configuration with Gigabit Ethernet and Thread support built in, whereas the first-generation 2017 box launched at $179 for 32GB or $199 for 64GB. While ad-heavy streaming sticks and budget set-top boxes often ship with tight memory and storage pools like 2GB of RAM and 8GB of flash, the new Apple TV 4K costs noticeably more than prior Apple TV generations—making it a stronger fit for frequent viewers than casual watchers.

In everyday testing, the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K felt responsive even alongside recent models, booting quickly, opening apps smoothly, and starting streams on services like Hulu and Netflix almost right away. Moving up from the 2017 model—or an older Apple TV HD—makes that speed gap even clearer across menus, app switching, and media playback.

Alongside faster internals, the 2026 chassis trims size and weight compared with the original 2017 unit:

Apple rates the A19 chip for up to 50% faster CPU performance and up to 2x faster GPU performance over the previous generation rather than the 2017 box. Reportedly paired with 8GB of RAM instead of the 2017 model’s 3GB, the extra headroom supports snappier multitasking and smoother gameplay in demanding Apple Arcade titles, especially fast-paced racing games with dense environments.

Connecting over Wi-Fi 7 on the 6 GHz band of an eero Pro 7 router allowed the fourth-generation Apple TV 4K to stream large 4K HDR movies from Plex without buffering, where an earlier model had struggled over the local network in a room without a convenient wired Ethernet drop.

Even so, wireless speed is only part of the picture. Older Apple TV 4K models lacked hardware AV1 decoding, meaning certain Plex files could require transcoding or encoding during playback. If your local media library relies on heavy high-bitrate files or modern codecs, both Wi-Fi 7 and newer media decoding hardware help reduce bottlenecks.

Unlike the 2017 unit, the 2026 Apple TV 4K builds in three far-field microphones—positioned on the front, left, and right with voice isolation—to support hands-free Siri commands and assist with tuning HomePod spatial audio.

Being able to speak without picking up the remote makes it easy to pause when a call or visitor interrupts, wake the TV, jump to the latest episode, play the next item in a watchlist, check smart home devices, and ask follow-up questions in a more natural flow. With Siri AI, on-screen awareness currently applies to Apple TV shows, while questions about other movies or series draw on general knowledge—identifying a character from title and timestamp context rather than reading the picture directly.

The updated Siri Remote adds Find My with Precision Finding plus a built-in speaker that plays a chime when triggered from a HomePod or the Apple TV 4K—and you can prompt Siri to play the sound again if you are still hunting for it.

In practical testing, the locator chime remained audible even when tucked under a couch blanket. Crucially, you do not have to buy the 2026 streaming box just to get that convenience, as the new Siri Remote works with almost any older Apple TV.

The fourth-generation Apple TV 4K expands speaker pairing to support four HomePods as surround speakers, using matching front and rear pairs of second-generation full-size HomePods or HomePod mini 2 units. Whole-room playback can also send the same audio across all four speakers to keep sports commentary clear around a space or keep dialogue intelligible at low volume when kids are sleeping.

Adding rear channels creates a noticeably wider, more enveloping spatial soundstage than a front two-speaker pair alone, bringing ambient effects and offscreen cues from behind the seating area.

For 2017 owners, the biggest takeaway is how familiar the Apple TV 4K experience stays in daily operation despite a smaller, lighter enclosure. The strongest arguments for upgrading from the 2017 model are faster app performance, the A19 chip, and Wi-Fi 7 streaming—including buffer-free Plex playback—rather than features available elsewhere. Because Siri AI is also supported on a third-generation box and the new Siri Remote works with almost any older Apple TV, those pieces do not require replacing your streamer. For heavy viewers, the 2026 model is a clear step up from 2017, though waiting for a sale makes sense if $299 is hard to justify right now.

Only 1.7% of scientists admit to plagiarism, yet 30% say they know a colleague who has plagiarized, and AI has made the line harder to see. In research, avoiding plagiarism means crediting others’ words and ideas, while AI disclosure explains how AI helped. As reported by Andy Stapleton, that help can include planning, generating keywords and outlining, not just producing complete drafts. You’ll learn how to distinguish these obligations and describe AI’s contribution, as well as understand what you remain responsible for when your name goes on a paper.

Stapleton’s rule has three parts: credit every source, disclose every AI use and own every word. Sources must be credited for their words and ideas, including when those ideas are paraphrased. A 2024 paper found that 59% of students felt unsure about subtler uses of AI. Disclosure sits alongside citation and does not replace it. In a 2023 study, AI detectors falsely flagged 61% of essays by non-native English speakers as AI-generated.

Plagiarism predates chatbots, and its established forms still matter when you use AI in research. AI makes plagiarism easier than ever and adds a new dimension to the five traditional types. It also raises a separate question: beyond whether you credited a source, how much help did you receive in producing the work?

These distinctions apply to students and researchers alike, and both teachers and university students have been caught copy-pasting. You need to credit the source of an idea even when you write the final sentence in your own words.

Discover other guides from our vast content that could be of interest on AI models and plagiarism.

A chatbot can produce a document in place of a paid writer, but requesting a document is not the same as writing it. Stapleton considers presenting an AI-generated document as your own writing a form of cheating. In 2018, 15.7% of students admitted paying someone to produce their work, showing that handing in work produced by someone else was a problem before chatbots.

AI can also help with narrower tasks, such as generating ideas, outlining a structure, producing keywords or creating a scaffold for an abstract. Those uses fall into a less clear area than directly generating and copying a document. Universities are struggling to distinguish AI use from plagiarism and other breaches of academic integrity.

A 2024 paper found clear disapproval of directly generating and copying AI content, while 59% of students felt unsure about subtler uses.

A citation credits another person’s work or ideas; AI disclosure explains the assistance a tool provided. Disclosure sits alongside citation and does not replace it. Falsely denying AI use is an integrity problem comparable to conventional plagiarism.

Match your description to the task. If AI helped you plan a presentation or produce an initial structure, say you used it for planning. If you went back and forth with it to develop ideas, describe that collaboration. If you used tools such as MCP connectors, which link an AI model to outside sources, to explore a research field, identify that use.

Disclosure also applies to generated material. Fully generated content can be acceptable for internal use within a team, but not when you present it publicly as your own work. Disclosure tells readers what role AI played rather than leaving them to assume you produced every part without it.

Disclosure is not an admission of guilt: the issue is whether you make the use clear, not simply whether you used a tool. Other studies found that revealing AI assistance reduced how people perceived the value of the work or contribution. Stapleton believes that cultural penalty needs to change.

AI detectors can make mistakes in both directions. In a 2023 study, 61% of essays by non-native English speakers were falsely flagged as AI-generated, while text combining human and AI writing can also pass detectors in 2026.

Paraphrasing software can change text at the click of a button and readily evade plagiarism detection, but it can also leave detectable fingerprints. Figures from a 2023 workshop put the number of papers flagged as AI at nearly 12,000, which Stapleton links to paraphrasing tools. This creates a cat-and-mouse contest between those tools and detection systems.

Patterns in word use can draw attention to AI-assisted writing, but they are not proof of plagiarism. Figures show a 28-fold rise in one frequently used term, “delves,” a 13-fold rise in “underscores” and a 10.7-fold rise in “showcasing,” while around 14% of abstracts show signs of large language model use. Text from models such as Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s tools can contain word-use fingerprints that machines can detect even when human readers would not notice them.

In Stapleton’s own earlier detector tests, making generated text into personal writing got around detection in every case tested, including by removing expressions or formatting uncharacteristic of one’s own writing. Those tests need updating, however, because detection algorithms have improved. He does not recommend rewriting generated text as a way to evade plagiarism rules.

AI assistance does not transfer responsibility for a paper to the tool. A paper Stapleton cites distinguishes between giving up control over part of a task and giving up responsibility for the result. His own rule has three parts: credit every source, disclose every AI use and own every word. Owning it means you have read it, agree with it and have checked it for factual accuracy.

The strongest point, in our view, is that a disclosure rule still works where detection fails. It rests on honesty rather than on catching anyone, which makes it the only standard that can realistically keep up with fast-changing tools. The 2023 study’s false flags on 61% of non-native English essays show how unreliable detection can be. We would check the exact AI policy of your university or journal before relying on any general advice. Disclosure is the common thread, but what counts as enough detail, and what is allowed at all, can differ between places.

Putting your name to AI-assisted research still means answering for what it says, not just explaining how it was produced. You can hand over parts of a task without handing over the final judgment about what belongs in your paper. For students and researchers who want to make that division clear, task-specific AI disclosure is a method well worth trying.

AI in Academic Research: Credit and Disclosure Credit Sources for Words and Ideas Verbatim plagiarism: copying someone else’s words and presenting them without credit. You can use an exact quotation if you credit its source; an unattributed sentence can be found through a search engine or plagiarism checker. Patchwork plagiarism: combining text and information from several sources while keeping their words or structure, without proper attribution. It is harder to police because the material comes from many places. Paraphrasing without a citation: putting someone else’s work or ideas into your own words and leaving out where they came from. Changing the wording does not remove your obligation to cite. Global plagiarism: passing off work produced entirely by someone else as your own. Self-plagiarism: presenting your earlier work as new research. You can refer to findings from a previous study, but not copy an old paragraph and claim it as new. Which Claude 3 AI model is best? If you want to pan around maps, tap playback controls, or sketch quick edits directly on your laptop display, Apple’s newly released touchscreen MacBook Pro brings Multi-Touch input to macOS for the first time. A 14-inch M5 Pro configuration tailored for on-the-go AI workloads came out to £4,200 in Better Creating’s hands-on breakdown video featured below, though touch input alone is more of a convenience than a standalone reason to upgrade. Buyers also face choices between standard glossy and nano-texture glass (with standard glass saving £150) alongside steep memory and storage upgrade tiers. Read on to see how the touchscreen OLED panel feels in daily use and how different M5 Pro and M5 Max configurations stack up on price.

Touchscreen usability: Touch feels responsive and intuitive in apps like Apple Maps and Pixelmator, though it works best as a supplement rather than a core buying reason. OLED display & flicker: The tandem OLED panel delivers high brightness and contrast, with Notebookcheck measuring 240 Hz PWM flicker on a tested 14-inch unit. Entry & build pricing: The touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro starts at £2,900 ($2,899 in the US), while Better Creating’s AI-focused M5 Pro build reached £4,200 and M5 Max builds start at £5,000. Glass finish trade-off: Choosing standard glass saves £150 ($150) over nano-texture glass while preserving deeper black saturation. Refined chassis: A slightly stiffer hinge minimizes screen wobble when tapping, and the 14-inch M5 Pro feels noticeably lighter than the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro.

Apple’s MacBook Pro line relied on essentially the same industrial silhouette for roughly five years. The new 14-inch M5 Pro model with the tandem PROLED XDR touchscreen preserves that recognizable profile while introducing targeted hardware updates beneath the surface.

In real-world testing, the touchscreen responds smoothly and feels natural for quick, direct interactions—especially when zooming or panning inside Apple Maps. It also comes in handy for tapping media controls inside Dynamic Island, sliding volume levels, flicking through long web pages, or sketching directly with a finger in Pixelmator.

Even so, macOS remains fundamentally built around a keyboard and Force Touch trackpad. Better Creating treats touch input as a welcome secondary convenience for occasional gestures rather than an essential reason to replace an otherwise capable Mac.

Switching to a tandem OLED display brings self-emissive pixels, deep blacks, and high HDR brightness, though OLED panels can trigger headaches or eye fatigue for sensitive viewers. One common culprit is pulse-width modulation (PWM), which cycles screen brightness rapidly at a frequency separate from the display’s refresh rate—with Notebookcheck measuring 240 Hz flicker on a tested 14-inch configuration.

Shoppers must also decide between standard glossy glass and a matte nano-texture finish:

The touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro starts at £2,900 (carrying a roughly $400 premium in the US over comparable non-OLED configurations). From there, configure-to-order upgrades climb rapidly depending on your CPU, GPU, unified memory, and SSD requirements.

For a compact travel setup geared toward running local AI tools, Better Creating configured a 14-inch M5 Pro with an 18-core CPU, the top 20-core GPU, and 48 GB of unified memory (double the entry allocation), adding a £500 storage upgrade to reach £4,200. Extra GPU cores make a tangible difference when running AI inference locally, while fast internal SSD throughput keeps large project files responsive.

Stepping up to the M5 Max unlocks up to 40 GPU cores and higher memory bandwidth for demanding 8K video editing and larger language models, starting at £5,000 with 48 GB of memory. Pushing memory to 64 GB lifts the total to £5,500, 128 GB reaches £7,000, and maxing out storage at 16 TB takes the build all the way to £14,000. For context on long-term value, a five-year-old M1 Max MacBook Pro originally costing around £3,400 fetched roughly £685 on trade-in.

To keep the screen steady when poked or swiped, Apple fitted the new MacBook Pro with a slightly stiffer hinge that noticeably reduces display wobble compared with earlier non-touch models.

Subtle refinements to chassis depth and edge contouring also trim bulk. Held side by side against the 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro, the 14-inch M5 Pro model feels noticeably lighter—making it easier to carry in a daily backpack without sacrificing ports or thermal headroom.

The touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro makes the most sense if you are coming from an older Apple Silicon machine like an M1-era laptop and want a lighter chassis, OLED contrast, and stronger GPU headroom for years ahead. If you already own a recent MacBook Pro—or are tempted mainly by the novelty of tapping the screen—the high entry price and steep upgrade ladder are harder to justify.

Anthropic’s November updates take Claude well beyond writing answers, adding tools that join your meetings, build spreadsheets and help you plan your spending. Claude can now read up to two years of bank transactions to help you plan spending, but it cannot move your money. Other additions turn conversations into shared spreadsheets, meeting notes and dashboards, while access depends on your subscription and organization’s settings. You’ll see how these additions work and where their limits matter, as Zinho Automates shows what’s available across Claude’s expanding workspace.

Fable 5.2 is the flagship model on every paid plan and is said to be up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1. Claude Meetings is rolling out in beta to Team and Enterprise subscribers, producing notes, transcripts and action items for Google Meet calls. Claude Data is out of beta on every paid plan and creates interactive dashboards from connected data sources. Claude Sheets is in beta on paid plans, with more than 250 functions and support for more than 500,000 populated cells, according to Anthropic. Claude Personal Finance is in beta for US Pro, Max and Ultra subscribers, with read-only access to up to two years of transactions.

Anthropic’s Claude combines a conversational assistant with tools for creating and editing work. Its November updates add features for individual subscribers and organizations, although access varies by plan and product. If you use Claude only for quick questions, much of that functionality remains unused.

Fable 5.2 launched as Anthropic’s flagship model and is the top model on every paid plan. Zinho Automates describes it as up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1 and cheaper through the API, although more expensive than Opus 5.5.

Claude Meetings was announced on November 10, 2026 and began rolling out in beta on November 12 for Team and Enterprise subscribers. It works with Google Meet through Claude’s web and desktop apps, and Anthropic plans to support other conferencing platforms.

Claude joins as a visible participant, announces itself in chat and produces notes, a transcript and action items. Participants can ask questions aloud or in chat, and Claude replies in writing by default. It can also create documents, whiteboards, presentations and other artifacts that colleagues can edit during the call. Zinho Automates expects meeting notes and real-time plans to save teams many hours a week.

After the call, a dedicated page holds the transcript and work, and invited organization members receive recap emails. In a later Claude conversation, you can ask about accessible past meetings. With permission, Claude can use tools connected to participants’ accounts, although spoken requests that use those tools require identity confirmation.

An organization owner must allow Google Calendar access before members can connect their calendars. You can invite Claude manually or set it to attend all meetings, with an option to exclude one-to-one calls; owners cannot set that preference for individuals. Meetings is on by default for Team, which supports organizations with 2 to 150 members, while an owner must activate it for Enterprise.

Discover other guides from our vast content that could be of interest on Claude Artifacts and features.

Anthropic asks users to obtain participants’ agreement to transcription. You can pause Claude’s listening or remove it, and a call can last up to eight hours. Claude stores transcripts, summaries and descriptions of screen content, but not audio recordings.

Team permits external guests by default, while Enterprise defaults to internal meetings. Where guests are not allowed, Claude leaves when an outsider joins. External guests’ contributions can appear in transcripts, but they cannot access the meeting page or recap emails, and Claude does not post answers in chats containing external guests.

During the beta, notes, transcripts and answers that do not use connected tools cost no extra, while connected-tool use counts against the requesting user’s allowance. Meeting-generated artifacts are free through February 10, 2027. Organizations using zero data retention, HIPAA-ready configurations or customer-managed encryption keys cannot use the beta.

Anthropic paused automatic attendance after call-joining problems in November. It reported normal joining operations on November 19 and restored automatic attendance to all Enterprise customers and some Team customers.

Claude Data, formerly Claude Dashboards, is out of beta on every paid plan. It uses a connected source, such as a CRM or analytics tool, to create an interactive dashboard from a prompt.

You can share a dashboard with your team and use its edit history to restore an earlier version if a change does not work. When the numbers are already available, you do not need to build the dashboard in pivot tables.

Claude Whiteboards is in beta on paid plans and lets a team edit a shared board. You can paste rough notes into Claude and ask it to arrange them into sections, giving collaborators a starting point for planning.

A board can also be created during a meeting. For plans that need costs or dates tracked in cells, Claude Sheets offers a spreadsheet instead.

Claude Sheets is a native spreadsheet application in Claude’s Artifacts feature, rather than an assistant embedded in Excel or Google Sheets. It launched in beta on November 10 and is available on paid plans across the web, desktop, iOS and Android.

You can describe a spreadsheet in a conversation or choose the Sheets template in Artifacts. Claude can create tabs, formulas and dropdowns, then highlight individual cells it changes in response to a chat request. You can edit cells yourself while Claude and collaborators work on the same sheet.

Sheets supports conditional formatting, checkboxes, sorting, filtering, cell history and version restoration, as well as bar, line and pie charts. It can generate formulas from descriptions and propose fixes for formula errors. Anthropic says it includes more than 250 functions and can hold more than 500,000 populated cells.

Sheets start private. Colleagues in the same organization can leave cell comments, but external collaborators cannot. Anyone with the link gives viewing access only and requires viewers to sign in to Claude, while Team and Enterprise restrict artifact sharing to their organization by default.

Existing work can be imported, exported or transferred to partner apps:

Sheets’ initial release lacks multi-select dropdowns, PDF export, macros, VBA, Power Query, DAX and print layouts. It cannot pull live data from connected apps or provide data to Claude documents, presentations or dashboards. Zinho Automates recommends Claude for Excel instead for heavy models or huge data sets; Claude for Google Workspace puts Claude inside Google Sheets.

For Team and Enterprise, Artifacts must be active, with cloud code execution and file creation turned on. Administrators manage the template under Organization settings → Artifacts → Templates. Enterprise can restrict it by group, and disabling a template leaves existing artifacts intact. Sheets is unavailable to organizations using HIPAA-ready configurations or zero data retention for Claude Code, and Sheets itself is not covered by zero data retention.

Claude Personal Finance launched in beta for US subscribers on Pro, Max and Ultra. It connects bank and card accounts through Plaid: you sign in directly with your bank and choose which accounts Claude can see.

Claude receives read-only access to up to two years of transactions and cannot move money. It can separate fixed and flexible spending, then use those figures to help map a month-by-month savings plan or find hotels within a budget. Anthropic recommends checking important numbers with your bank.

Claude Interactive Connectors arrived on November 10 and are rolling out to all plans, starting on the web and desktop. They open full versions of apps such as Notion or Adobe alongside chat or full screen, so you can watch changes appear as Claude makes them.

We think Claude Personal Finance deserves the most attention because it asks for the most trust. Even with read-only access and no ability to move money, letting an AI see up to two years of bank and card transactions is a bigger step than asking it to draft notes or build a spreadsheet. We think Meetings suits teams that already live in Google Meet and lose time to note-taking, given its notes, transcripts and action items. It is a poor fit for anyone on a personal plan or using another call platform, since neither is covered yet.

You can now take a discussion beyond an answer and into shared work that colleagues can keep editing. Which parts of that workflow you can use will be determined by your subscription and your organization’s permissions. If you want help turning conversations and rough ideas into plans you can work on together, Claude’s workspace tools are worth checking out in more detail.

Bloomberg Technoz, Jakarta – Pengelola jaringan stasiun pengisian bahan bakar umum (SPBU) BP-AKR, PT Aneka Petroindo Raya (APR), mengatakan strategi penyusunan kuota impor bahan bakar minyak (BBM) 2027 akan bertumpu pada proyeksi pertumbuhan jaringan gerai dan kebutuhan pelanggan.

Langkah tersebut ditempuh guna menyiasati ekspansi bisnis ritel perseroan di tengah dinamika pasokan bahan bakar yang belum cukup jelas untuk badan usaha (BU) hilir migas swasta.

“Saya meminta agar situasi ini segera diselidiki. Ini bukan kesalahan kecil, melainkan kesalahan besar yang dilakukan dengan sengaja,” tambah presiden dalam unggahan yang dikirim dari lapangan golf miliknya di West Palm Beach pada pagi hari libur Thanksgiving AS.

Bloomberg Technoz, Jakarta - Pertumbuhan laba di perusahaan-perusahaan industri China mencapai level tertinggi dalam lima bulan pada bulan Oktober. Permintaan produk kecerdasan buatan terus menopang harga.

Laba industri meningkat 20,1% bulan lalu dibandingkan tahun sebelumnya, menurut data yang diterbitkan oleh Biro Statistik Nasional pada Jumat. Angka ini lebih kuat daripada proyeksi kenaikan 15,5% oleh Bloomberg Economics. Untuk 10 bulan pertama tahun ini, pendapatan bersih naik 16%.

Ini adalah bulan kedua berturut-turut pertumbuhan laba meningkat, karena inflasi industri meningkat akibat kenaikan harga komoditas termasuk minyak, serta penjualan perangkat keras AI yang didorong oleh booming pusat data global. Peningkatan dari kenaikan harga lebih dari mengimbangi pertumbuhan produksi yang lebih lambat.

“Permintaan akan daya komputasi AI terus meningkat, mendorong pertumbuhan laba yang berkelanjutan di sektor chip penyimpanan dan sektor manufaktur terkait,” kata analis NBS Yu Weining dalam sebuah pernyataan yang menyertai rilis data tersebut.

Ledakan AI, bersamaan dengan permintaan dari sektor energi terbarukan, telah membantu mendorong kenaikan harga mineral seperti tembaga dan aluminium tahun ini, kata Yu.
